name: SimpleMem

paper.title: SimpleMem: Efficient Lifelong Memory for LLM Agents

construction.unit: atomic memory unit: self-contained factual statement with metadata
construction.processing: LLM gate drops low-info windows; coreference and ISO-8601 time normalisation; atomisation

organization.stores: one LanceDB store with three index views
organization.index: Qwen3-embedding-0.6b dense + BM25 sparse + metadata (time, entities, topic, salience)

management.operations: online semantic synthesis merges related units within session before commit
management.conflicts: answer prompt prioritises most recent memory unit

retrieval.query: LLM planner writes semantic, lexical and temporal queries plus complexity/depth
retrieval.candidates: top-n per view: cosine, BM25, metadata constraint filter
retrieval.selection: set union of the three views, deduplicated
retrieval.budget: n proportional to inferred depth, range 3-20 (Table 7)

use.context: abstract representations plus detailed units, ordered by relevance
use.reasoning: single answer call; recency-first conflict rule; abstain if missing

stages.ingestion: Dialogue is cut into overlapping sliding windows (20 turns, stride 5); an LLM-based implicit semantic-density gate emits nothing for low-information windows (e.g. phatic chit-chat).
stages.construction: For informative windows a single LLM pass (gpt-4.1-mini) extracts context-independent atomic memory units with coreference resolved and relative times converted to absolute ISO-8601 timestamps.
stages.organization: Each unit is indexed in three views in LanceDB: dense embedding (Qwen3-embedding-0.6b), BM25 sparse lexical index, and symbolic metadata (timestamp, entities, topic, salience) for SQL-style filtering; flat store.
stages.update: Online Semantic Synthesis consolidates related fragments within the current session into unified higher-density entries before they are written (v1 described this as asynchronous recursive consolidation).
stages.retrieval: An LLM planner infers search intent and emits semantic, lexical and symbolic queries plus a depth d; each view returns top-n (n proportional to d, range 3-20) and results are merged by set union.
stages.answer: The merged, deduplicated context is passed to the backbone LLM for answer generation.

summary: Compresses dialogue at write time into atomic, time-normalised memory units indexed in dense, BM25 and metadata views, and uses an LLM planner to set per-query retrieval depth, cutting query tokens to about 530-580.
notes:
Annotated from the current arXiv HTML (fetched 2026-09-28); v1 used the stage names Recursive Memory Consolidation / Adaptive Query-Aware Retrieval and had no LongMemEval table; LoCoMo tables are numerically identical across v1 and the current version. Paper uses the ICML template but no acceptance is stated. AXES-CHECK: 'semantic + lexical + symbolic' in the seed taxonomy's write-time column is really the indexing (organisation) step; the write-time processing in the paper is LLM gating/filtering + atomic extraction with coreference and timestamp normalisation + intra-session synthesis (consolidation).
DESIGN: Sec 2.1-2.3, Sec 3.1, App. A.1-A.3, App. B.2 (Table 7).
